subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 4: Vocabulary and Grammar – Hobbies and be good at
outcomes: I can say hobby phrases like bake a cake, fix toys and do experiments.
I can talk about ability: I'm good at juggling. I'm terrible at spelling.
I can ask and answer: Is he good at counting? Yes, he is.

tf.s: After "good at" we use verb + -ing: good at baking.
"She's terrible at throw a ball" is correct.
tf.why: We need -ing: She's terrible at throwing a ball.

tf.s: Great at is better than good at.
tf.why: Right! The scale is great at, good at, not very good at, terrible at.

tf.s: Terrible at means you do something very well.
tf.why: Terrible at means you are very bad at it.
Yes! These are hobby phrases from the lesson.

tf.s: The -ing form of bake is bakeing.
The -ing form of juggle is juggling.
tf.why: Great! Drop the e and add -ing.

tf.s: We say "make a cake" and "bake a pizza" in this lesson.
tf.why: The phrases are bake a cake and make a pizza.

tf.s: "Is he good at spelling?" "No, he isn't." is a correct short answer.
tf.why: Yes! Is he …? No, he isn't.

tf.s: "Not very good at" is the worst on the scale.

boxes.why: good at + verb-ing; drop the e.
In the lesson we count fingers.

boxes.q: Is Thamer good at throwing a ball? Yes, ___.
Which is the best on the scale?
boxes.why: Great at is the top of the scale.

mcq.q: Put in order from best to worst.
o: great at, good at, not very good at, terrible at
good at, great at, terrible at, not very good at
terrible at, good at, great at, not very good at
not very good at, great at, good at, terrible at
mcq.why: Great at is the best and terrible at is the worst.

mcq.q: Which list has only hobby phrases from the lesson?
o: fix toys, juggle, bake a cake
mcq.why: These are hobbies; the others are appearance, personality or days.
Great at and good at talk about ability.

mcq.q: Make a question: Shihab / spell a really long word
o: Is Shihab good at spelling a really long word?
Does Shihab good at spell a really long word?
Is Shihab good at spell a really long word?
Shihab is good spelling a really long word?

mcq.q: Thamer is great at throwing a ball a long way. Answer: Is Thamer good at throwing a ball a long way?
o: Yes, he is. He's great at throwing a ball a long way.
No, he isn't. He's terrible at it.
mcq.why: He is great at it, so the answer is Yes, he is.

mcq.q: Samar acts very, very well. What do you report?
mcq.why: Very, very well = great at + verb-ing.

mcq.q: Find the mistake: "I'm not very good at make a pizza."
mcq.why: After at we use verb-ing: making.

mcq.q: Saif is good at fixing toys but he isn't very good at juggling. Which is true?
o: Saif fixes toys better than he juggles.
Saif juggles better than he fixes toys.
Saif is terrible at fixing toys.
mcq.why: Good at is higher on the scale than not very good at.

mcq.q: Why do we write "baking" and not "bakeing"?
mcq.why: Verbs ending in e drop it: bake → baking.
